title: Keeping Momentum in Faith — Hebrews 12:1
paragraphs:
He didn’t say the race would be short.
He said run.
Hebrews 12:1 is not a verse for spectators. It is for the tired. The distracted. The believer who still loves Jesus but feels the drag of hidden weight, old wounds, and quiet compromise.
“Let us throw off everything that hinders and the sin that so easily entangles… and let us run with perseverance the race marked out for us.”

Because not everything slowing you down is evil. Some things are just heavy. Some habits. Some friendships. Some patterns. Some fears you’ve carried so long, you started calling them personality instead of bondage.

God never told you to win this race by pretending to be strong. He told you to lay things down and keep your eyes on Jesus. The Christian life is not about flashy starts. It is about holy endurance. Step by step. Prayer by prayer. Obedience by obedience. When your knees are weak and your heart is shaking, grace still says, “Keep going.”
And that’s where the Gospel walks in.

Because Jesus did not just point at the finish line. He ran ahead of us, carried the cross, endured the shame, crushed the grave, and now strengthens every weary runner who trusts in Him. Your momentum in faith is not powered by human hype. It is sustained by the finished work of Christ.

So breathe. Repent. Drop the weight.
And run again.
There is still grace for your next step.

Prayer:
Lord Jesus, strip away every weight that slows me down and every sin that entangles my soul. Teach me to run with endurance, with my eyes fixed on You. When I feel tired, be my strength. When I feel ashamed, be my covering. Keep me moving in faith until I finish well. Amen.
